```{python}
d = json.loads(data_path.read_text())
DIMS = [("volumen", "Volume"), ("realizado", "Realized"), ("despliegue", "Deployment"),
        ("capacidad", "Capability"), ("riesgo", "Risk"), ("gobernanza", "Governance"),
        ("promocional", "Promotional"), ("especificidad", "Specificity")]

def fmt(c):
    p_str = "p<0.01" if c["p"] < 0.01 else f"p={c['p']:.2f}"
    cell = f"{c['beta_std']:+.2f} ({p_str})"
    return f"**{cell}**" if c["p"] < 0.05 else cell

coefs = d["outcomes"]["beta"]["coeficientes_M2"]
table = [[dim_label, fmt(coefs[dim_key])] for dim_key, dim_label in DIMS]
Markdown(tabulate(table, headers=["Content dimension", "Beta"]))
```

**AI-washing index, full specification.** $\text{Substance}_{it} = \log(1 + n_{\text{activities},it}) \times \text{Grounding}_{it}$, where $\text{Grounding}_{it}$ averages, with empirical-Bayes shrinkage per component, five concreteness markers over that firm-year's disclosed activities (named function, deployed/scaled stage, named product or process, quantified outcome, named provider). $W_{it} = \text{pctrank}(\text{Disclosure}_{it}) - \text{pctrank}(\text{Substance}_{it})$, where $\text{Disclosure}_{it}$ is AI frames per 1,000 words and both percentile ranks are computed within the analytical sample (firm-years with $\text{Disclosure}_{it} > 0$: 1,449 of 2,475 firm-years, 474 of 510 firms pooled 2021–2025). No regression, no fixed effects, no fitted residual: it is a rank-based gap between two independently extracted quantities.

Percentile rank rather than z-score standardization: with z-scores, $\text{Disclosure}_{it}$'s distribution has a far heavier right tail than $\text{Substance}_{it}$'s (maximum z of 13.7 against 3.7), which put firms with the *most* grounded activity in absolute terms (Microsoft, NVIDIA) in the washing tail whenever their disclosure happened to be an even bigger outlier than their already-large substance — Spearman between the z-score and percentile-rank versions of $W$ is 0.988, but the specific firm-years in the top 5% differ, and only the percentile version keeps the tail composed of firms with no grounded activity behind unusually heavy disclosure.

**Substance functional form.** An additive form, $z(\log(1+n_{\text{activities}})) + z(\text{Grounding})$, and a grounded-count form, $\log(1 + n_{\text{activities}} \times \text{Grounding})$, were both compared against the multiplicative form used here. Substance under the multiplicative and grounded-count forms correlates at Spearman = 0.993 (n = 1,449), and the resulting $W$ at Spearman = 0.988, with 66 of 73 top-5%-tail firm-years shared between the two (Jaccard = 0.825). The multiplicative form is used because it does not reward raw activity count over grounding quality when the two trade off directly against each other (a firm with many but poorly grounded activities does not automatically outscore one with fewer but well-grounded activities, at typical values in this sample), while the grounded-count form's arithmetic can favor the larger, less-grounded firm in exactly that comparison.

**Alternative firm-year aggregation.** Results are unchanged when firm-year intensity is constructed as an aggregate-numerator-over-aggregate-denominator ratio rather than the median document rate: the two rollups are numerically identical across all seven content dimensions and 2,475 firm-years (max absolute difference below 1e-9), because a firm-year's AI content comes from a single dominant filing often enough that the rollup rule carries no weight in practice.

## Appendix F: Variable construction {.unnumbered}

| Financial concept | Coverage of the firm-year panel |
|---|---:|
| Revenue | 99% |
| Net margin | 99% |
| Capex | 91% |
| SG&A | 81% |
| R&D expense | 46% (1,318 of 2,868 firm-years; outcome only) |

: XBRL concept coverage. {#tbl-d1-xbrl-coverage}

Fiscal-period alignment rules (period-end date matched to the nearest prior filing date; the [340, 380]-day validity window for year-over-year growth), the market-model beta and idiosyncratic-volatility construction (252 trading days pre-filing, one-factor market model), and the ROIC-minus-WACC construction (geometric equity risk premium of 6.48%, not arithmetic) are documented here.

### R&D coverage and interpretation

R&D expense is constructed from four comparable current-expense concepts: `us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense`, `us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpenseExcludingAcquiredInProcessCost`, `us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpenseSoftwareExcludingAcquiredInProcessCost`, and `ifrs-full:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense`. The latter two recover software reporters and IFRS filers that the narrower US-GAAP mapping missed; they add 34 firm-years to the panel. The resulting measure is available for 1,318 of 2,868 firm-years (46.0%).

This is not evidence that the remaining firms spend zero on R&D. In a SIC-based diagnostic grouping, separately reported R&D is common among manufacturing and software firms (81.4% coverage) and almost absent in financial services and real estate (1.1%). The missingness is therefore primarily an economic and disclosure-selection feature of the accounting data, rather than a generic failure of the XBRL collection process. The raw stored facts contain no company-specific extension namespace, so this pipeline cannot recover issuer-defined R&D extensions from that input.

For that reason, R&D-to-sales is not imputed and is excluded from the common set of financial controls. When it is an outcome, estimates are interpreted for the non-random subsample of firms that separately disclose comparable current R&D; each specification reports its effective sample size. Tags for tax credits, capitalized development, acquired in-process R&D, and industry-specific exploration costs are deliberately not pooled into this measure because they do not represent the same current R&D expense.

### Market beta and estimation-window diagnostics

For each firm-year, market beta is estimated from a one-factor market model over the 252 trading days strictly before the actual filing date of the 10-K. Let $R_{i,t}$ denote the daily return on the firm's adjusted close, $R_{f,t}$ the daily risk-free rate, and $(\text{MKT} - \text{RF})_t$ the daily market excess return from the Ken French Fama--French three-factor file (`ff3_daily.parquet`). The estimated regression is

$$
R_{i,t} - R_{f,t} = \alpha_i + \beta_i (\text{MKT} - \text{RF})_t + \varepsilon_{i,t}.
$$

`build_market_factors.py` identifies the first trading day on or after the filing date and takes the preceding 252 price observations. It then retains only dates for which the firm return, $(\text{MKT} - \text{RF})_t$, and $R_{f,t}$ are all available, and estimates the intercept and slope by OLS. The code requires at least 120 valid daily observations (`BETA_MIN_OBS = 120`); otherwise beta is recorded as missing. The idiosyncratic-volatility measure uses the standard deviation of residuals from the same fitted model, annualized by $\sqrt{252}$.

The resulting `firm_year_market_factors.parquet` panel contains 2,762 firm-years for 477 tickers in 2021--2026. Beta is available for 2,739 observations (99.2%). The estimation-window diagnostic has a mean of 249.8 return days and a median of 252; 98.0% of estimates use at least 240 trading days. The remaining 23 firm-years have fewer than 120 valid observations and are retained with beta missing rather than receiving a short-window estimate. Among valid estimates, beta has mean 0.91, median 0.88, standard deviation 0.47, interquartile range 0.59--1.18, and range $[-0.31, 2.96]$.

Daily prices are collected from 2020-01-01, so early-2021 filings have a prior-year trading history available for the 252-day window. The sampling frame is built around S&P 500 membership frozen at 2021-12-31, supplemented by the manual core; 29 of the 517 firms in the current universe are explicitly marked `delisted`. Price collection first uses Yahoo Finance and then falls back to Stooq and Tiingo when a delisted ticker is unavailable. Freezing membership and retaining these firms reduces survivorship bias relative to a current-constituent sample, although historical price coverage still depends on the availability and adjustment quality of those fallback sources.

## Appendix G: Supplementary SEC dynamic difference-in-differences specifications {.unnumbered}

To evaluate the robustness of the regulatory scrutiny findings presented in Chapter 5, @tbl-g1-sec-multivariate reports the continuous dynamic difference-in-differences specification across all four disclosure dimensions: Operational Specificity, Quantified Outcome Claims, Promotional Framing, and Risk & Cautionary Framing.

Each regression estimates:

$$
Y_{it} = \alpha_i + \lambda_t + \sum_{k \neq -1} \beta_k \left( \widetilde{W}_i^{\text{pre}} \times \mathbf{1}[t = k] \right) + \mathbf{X}_{it}'\boldsymbol{\gamma} + \varepsilon_{it}
$$

across 5,376 firm-quarters (490 firms), where $\widetilde{W}_i^{\text{pre}}$ is the standardized pre-event decoupling intensity ($W_i^{\text{pre}}$ averaged over quarters prior to 2024Q1), $\alpha_i$ and $\lambda_t$ are firm and quarter fixed effects, and standard errors are clustered by firm.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-g1-sec-multivariate
#| tbl-cap: "SEC dynamic difference-in-differences specifications across four disclosure dimensions (5,376 firm-quarters, 490 firms)."
#| echo: false
import json
from pathlib import Path
from tabulate import tabulate
from IPython.display import Markdown

data_path = Path("../data/processed/clusters/sec_did_continuous.json")
if not data_path.exists():
    data_path = Path("data/processed/clusters/sec_did_continuous.json")
d = json.loads(data_path.read_text())

LABELS = {
    "spec_per_1k": "Operational Specificity",
    "quant_per_1k": "Quantified Outcome Claims",
    "promo_per_1k": "Promotional Framing",
    "risk_per_1k": "Risk & Cautionary Framing"
}

rows = []
for key, label in LABELS.items():
    res = d[key]
    pre_p = res["pre_p"]
    post_p = res["post_p"]
    post_mean = res["post_mean"]
    pre_str = f"{pre_p:.3f}" if pre_p >= 0.001 else "<0.001"
    post_str = f"{post_p:.3f}" if post_p >= 0.001 else "<0.001"
    mean_str = f"{post_mean:+.4f}"
    fails_pre = "Yes (p<0.05)" if pre_p < 0.05 else "No (Flat pre-trend)"
    sig_post = "Yes (p<0.05)" if post_p < 0.05 else "No (Null response)"
    rows.append([label, pre_str, fails_pre, post_str, sig_post, mean_str])

headers = ["Outcome Dimension", "Pre-trend p-val", "Pre-trend Test", "Post Joint p-val", "Post Response", "Mean Post Coeff. (per 1 SD W_pre)"]
Markdown(tabulate(rows, headers=headers))
```

*Notes:* Estimated on 5,376 firm-quarters (490 firms). Standard errors clustered by firm. The reference quarter is 2023Q4 ($k = -1$). Pre-trend test reports the $p$-value from an $F$-test of the joint hypothesis that all pre-event coefficients $\beta_k = 0$ for $k < -1$. Post joint test reports the $p$-value from an $F$-test that all post-event coefficients $\beta_k = 0$ for $k \ge 0$ (2024Q1--2025Q4). Mean post coefficient reports the simple average of $\beta_k$ across all post-shock quarters, expressing the quarterly change in claims per 1,000 words per 1 standard deviation increase in pre-event decoupling.
